_comment: Starter policy: two developer CLIs, codex and opencode. Copy it to dispatcher/policy.json (gitignored) and edit there. dispatcher/policy.full-roster.json carries every route ocli knows (agy, Muse, Cline Pass, Claude Opus, Astra); copy routes from it as you add CLIs. A route runs only when its status is "ok": probe it by hand once first. dispatch.mjs reads ORCHESTRA_POLICY, else dispatcher/policy.json, else this file. The models are the ones these routes were verified with; copy the file, set each model to one your CLI lists, and re-probe a route before you mark it ok. Placeholders: {model} {effort} {variant} {task} {root} {prompt}; any other {name} is rejected before spawn, and braces inside the prompt are left alone. The argv is passed as an array: the prompt never reaches a shell. The implement route ships with GLM-5.3 on the Z.ai coding plan; set its model to any id `opencode models` lists.

architect.note: Claude Code itself is the orchestrator; it does not dispatch to itself.

_notes: UNSAFE: --auto approves every permission request with no prompt, and opencode has no OS sandbox. --dir {root} sets where it works, not what it can reach: it can run commands, write outside {root}, use the network and your git credentials. See 'Permissions and sandboxing' in the README.
--auto: a headless run cannot answer permission prompts; without it a prompt can stall or be denied silently.
--pure: no external plugins or MCP servers at startup.
--dir {root}: without it, a relative path in the prompt was written relative to $HOME, not to the cwd the dispatcher spawns opencode in.
--variant: reasoning effort is a provider variant, not a separate model id. Check `opencode models` for the ids your providers expose.
--title {task}: names the session, so a later dispatch on the same task can resume it.
A session error is written to stdout only, as {type:'error', ...}, with stderr empty; dispatch treats it as the CLI's own refusal evidence.
-C {root}: an explicit working dir instead of relying on the spawn cwd.
-s workspace-write: codex's own OS sandbox confines writes to {root}, whatever the global sandbox setting is. This is the only shipped route with a real sandbox.
-o: the final message also lands in a file you can read back cleanly.
codex may stop and ask a scope question instead of guessing (exit 0, no changes): answer it in the brief and re-dispatch.
Usage is read from `codex app-server` (account/rateLimits/read) before and after each run; reading it spends no model allowance.
The codex default: GPT-6.1 Sol at xhigh (AA 51 in the shipped ranking). Replace the model with one your plan can reach; `codex debug models` lists them.

rotation._note: Which routes --role auto may pick, tie-broken in this order. Edit to the developers you actually use.
